title: Defect list, punch items and handover sign-off
audience: Cleaners and supervisors who compile the defect list and complete the handover after a post-construction clean.
learningOutcomes: Compile a defect list of marks, damage and incomplete items with their locations.
Separate cleaning items from items that belong to the trades.
Complete a handover sign-off that does not claim clearance or completion beyond the scope.

instruction.heading: The defect list
instruction.body: Walk each area once in a fixed order, usually from the top of the room downwards and from the entry around the room, so that nothing is missed. List every defect and punch item you can see within the scope you were given: marks and scuffs on walls and doors, scratches, chipped or cracked finishes, missing fittings or covers, residues that did not come off, incomplete trade work such as an unfinished edge, and any damage you think was caused during the build. Give each item a number, a location, a short factual description, and a photograph where the site permits it. Describe what you see, not why it happened. Mark each item as a cleaning item, a trade item, a damage item, or an unknown item that needs a decision. Cleaning items are yours to resolve within scope. Trade items belong to the responsible trade, and you name that trade on the list.

instruction.heading: Acceptance criteria before handover
instruction.body: Agree the acceptance criteria before the handover, in writing if you can. The criteria say what the cleaning must achieve in each area, which items are in scope, which are excluded, and who may approve exceptions. Check the work against those criteria, not against a general sense that it looks clean. A handover that depends on a verbal agreement is harder to defend, so write down any change that the client or site agrees to during the walk-through, with the time and the name of the person who agreed.

instruction.heading: The handover sign-off
instruction.body: Sign off only what you checked. The sign-off describes the cleaning that was done, the areas and criteria it covered, the defects and punch items listed, and the items not resolved, with the responsible person for each. It is not a clearance certificate, a building or regulatory sign-off, or a guarantee that the finish meets any standard that was not agreed. Do not write words such as defect-free, complete or approved unless each of those words is true for the scope you checked, and say which scope that is. Date and time the sign-off, and attach the list it refers to.

instruction.heading: Recording exceptions and keeping the list current
instruction.body: Record each exception and each unresolved item with the person responsible for it, and the date by which it is expected to be resolved if that has been agreed. Keep the list current. When an item is resolved, check it, record the check, and reissue the list rather than editing the old version. A handover that hides an open item is a false record, even if every other line is accurate. If you find a new defect after the sign-off, record it on a new list, and tell the person who signed.

procedure: Walk each area in a fixed order, and list every defect and punch item with a number, location and a factual description.
Mark each item as cleaning, trade, damage or unknown, and name the responsible trade or person.
Check the work against the acceptance criteria agreed in writing before the sign-off.
Sign off only the work that was checked, and list the exceptions and the unresolved items.
Keep the list current, and reissue it when items are resolved, with each check recorded.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks you to sign the handover while a paint scratch on a wall and a missing door handle are still on the list.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not sign the handover as complete. List the scratch and the missing handle with their locations and photographs. Mark the scratch as a trade or damage item and the handle as a trade item, and name the responsible trade for each. Sign off only the cleaning that was checked against the criteria, with both items listed as exceptions. Give the client a copy of the list.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks you to write on the form that the property is defect-free after your clean.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you write instead, and why?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not write defect-free. Write the scope you checked, the criteria, and the list of defects and exceptions. Under the consumer rules, a statement that gives a false or misleading picture can breach the law even if the writer had no intent to mislead, and any claim needs reasonable grounds. Explain the limit to the client and keep the list attached.

workedExamples.situation: During the walk-through you see a cracked floor tile near a water stain on the ceiling below a bathroom.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you record it, and what do you avoid saying?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record both as found, with location, description and photographs, and mark them as unknown items that need a decision by the responsible trade or the building maintenance contact. Do not state the cause of the water stain or the crack, and do not say the cleaning caused or repaired either one. Do not use a ladder or a platform to look at the high points unless your training and the site authorise it. Put the referral and the time in the list.

equipmentAndPpe: Defect and punch list template, numbered by area.
Acceptance criteria sheet, agreed in writing before the walk-through.
Camera or phone for defect photographs, used only where the site permits.
Torch for checking marks under a directional light.
Signature and date block for the sign-off, with a space for the list of exceptions.
Gloves and closed footwear as the site sets. Do not use a ladder or platform to inspect high points unless your training and the site authorise it.

commonErrors.error: Signing the handover with items still open.
commonErrors.prevention: List the open items with responsible persons, and sign off only what was checked.

commonErrors.error: Treating a trade defect as a cleaning item.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark each item as cleaning, trade, damage or unknown, and name the responsible trade.

commonErrors.error: Letting the sign-off read as a clearance, a certificate or a guarantee.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe only the cleaning done, the scope checked, and the list.

commonErrors.error: Editing an old list instead of reissuing it.
commonErrors.prevention: Reissue the list with a date, and record the check for each resolved item.

commonErrors.error: Relying on verbal agreements about exceptions.
commonErrors.prevention: Write each agreed exception on the list, with the time and the person who agreed.

commonErrors.error: Describing the cause of a defect in the list.
commonErrors.prevention: Record what is seen and where, and leave the cause to the responsible trade.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consumer claims. The ACCC states that claims must be accurate and backed by reasonable grounds, that a statement creating a false impression can breach the rules even if each word is accurate, that staying silent can mislead when a detail matters, and that intention does not matter (ACCC, false or misleading claims; page metadata 28 June 2026).

No certification authority. A cleaning sign-off is not a regulatory certificate, a building approval or a clearance. This lesson does not grant any authority to certify building work, a trade item, or the safety of a space.

Work at height during inspection. Do not use a ladder, scaffold or elevating platform to look at high points unless your training and the site authorise it. Use the site's access arrangements. The height rules for work at height are covered in the window cleaning track and in the official references there.
Photographs. Take photographs only where the site permits, and store them securely with the list.

qualityStandard: The defect list is complete for the scope, with a number, location and factual description for each item, and a photograph where permitted.
Each item is marked as cleaning, trade, damage or unknown, and the responsible trade or person is named.
The sign-off is limited to the work checked against the agreed criteria, and every exception is listed.
No sign-off wording describes the work as a clearance, a certificate or a guarantee.
documentationEvidence: Defect and punch list with numbers, locations, categories, responsible persons and photographs where permitted.
Acceptance criteria sheet agreed before the walk-through.
Handover sign-off with the date, time, scope checked and the list of exceptions attached.
Record of any verbal agreement, written up on the list with the time and person.
summary: List defects and punch items with locations, and mark each as cleaning, trade, damage or unknown.
Check against the agreed criteria, and sign off only what was checked.
Never sign with items hidden, and never describe the sign-off as a clearance.

knowledgeChecks.question: A paint scratch is found on a wall during handover. How is it recorded?
options: Listed with its location, and assigned to the responsible person
Ignored, because it is small and not a problem for the job site
Painted over by the cleaner without a record of it at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the cleaning sign-off confirm?
options: Regulatory clearance of the whole building for occupation by the new owner next week
The cleaning was checked against the agreed criteria, with exceptions listed
The building is finished in every respect, inside and out, as agreed with the client

knowledgeChecks.question: Should you sign while items are still open?
options: Yes, so the job can be finished on the day as planned
Yes, if the client insists in writing on the day and signs
No, list the open items and sign off only what was checked
